full_judgment: 8. It appears that by a number of notifications dated the 2nd April. 1956 published in the Dacca Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 2nd, April, 1956, all interests of all rent-receivers in their respective estates, taluks tenures holdings and tenancies situated in several districts including the district of Mymensingh were acquired with effect from 14th April, 1956. There is no dispute that hats and bazars were non-retainable khas lands. On the publication of the notifications, all non-retainable khas lands including hats in khas possession of a landlord vested absolutely in the Government free from encumbrances under section 3(4) of the S.A. &T Act. It is admitted on all hands that on the relevant date the Salimabad hat at Tebaria and the Sa lima bad Gohatta at Salimabad were in khas possession of the landlord and so the Salimabad hat at Tebaria which the defendants call Tebaria Chandganj hat and the plaintiffs call Salimabad Chandganj bat and the Salimabad Gobatta vested in the Government free from encumbrances. It was held in the case of Kali Charon Das and others Vs. Tamiruddin alias Jamiruddin and others reported in 10 DLR 523 relied on by Mr. Syed Isbtiaq Ahmed that the easements and customary rights of way are encumbrance and have been wiped out on such vesting. I do not see any reason why the customary right as claimed by the plaintiffs in the instant suit of compulsorily having the hat days on Tuesdays and Fridays will not also be -an encumbrance within the meaning of section 3(2) referred to above and be wiped out. Therefore even if the plaintiffs had the alleged customary right by immemorial user, it was wiped out on the vesting of the bat in the government free from encumbrances.
